note: Existing-source, strict-license-screened public gallery. Additional historical photos remain held from this site. Anatomy overlays are teaching annotations, not a separate verified voucher determination.

tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — SHORT BLUE-GREEN TUFT
tiles.details: Species panels 1–2 (indices 0–1) show a compact basal habit and curling dry blades; the new Jim Conrad Uvalde limestone-site panel 5 (index 4) independently shows small real tufts among rocks. Neither photograph exposes a connected rooted perennial crown. Kew reports 20–80 cm culms; trace a complete flowering stem before determining species.
tiles.short: Mostly basal stiff glaucous perennial bunch; old dry basal blades often curl.
tiles.status: REAL TARGET HABIT PHOTOS — ROOTED CROWN WITH SCALE NEEDED

tiles.heading: 02 · TRUE LIGULE AND LEAF COLLAR
tiles.details: Jim Conrad's source-authenticated Uvalde photograph (species panel 6, index 5) ACTUALLY SHOWS a white fringe of true ligule hairs at the blade/sheath junction, with the comparatively smooth green sheath below; two arrows target these visible tissues. This is genuine anatomical photo evidence but the original is unscaled, so the Kew species-level 1–1.5 mm hair-fringe length remains a PUBLISHED measurement, not photo-measured. A Williamson County subsp. filipes treatment describes a 1.2–1.5 mm membranous ciliate ligule and pale collar; do not impose subspecies-specific morphology or identity on this species-level photo. Still obtain a calibrated 1-mm collar image of a connected local specimen.
tiles.short: Kew: 1–1.5 mm fringe of hairs; verify at the blade–sheath junction.
tiles.status: ACTUAL TRUE LIGULE HAIR FRINGE PHOTO + TWO VISIBLE ARROWS; 1-MM SCALE AND CONNECTED HAYS VOUCHER MISSING

tiles.heading: 03 · OPEN BUT ORDERLY FLOWERING PANICLE
tiles.details: Species panel 3 (index 2) shows actual branch architecture and small attached spikelets, with existing arrows only on visible units. Kew reports appressed solitary spikelets; Williamson subsp. filipes specimens can show short paired stalks, so do not force an unexamined subspecies arrangement onto this species card. A very diffuse detached/tumbling annual head suggests P. capillare instead.
tiles.short: Pyramidal 6–20 cm panicle with relatively stiff ascending branches.
tiles.status: REAL ARCHIVED BRANCH PHOTO — NO MEASURED DISSECTION

tiles.heading: 04 · SPIKELET, GLUMES, LEMMA AND AWNS
tiles.details: Species-level Kew GrassBase describes dorsally compressed ovate two-floret spikelets, five-veined lower and upper glumes, a basal sterile floret and an upper fertile floret with shiny dark-brown hardened lemma ~2–3.5 mm. The fertile lemma is awnless. The Williamson County subsp. filipes treatment gives DIFFERENT narrower measurements and glume-vein counts; keep those subspecies-specific. Species panel 4 (index 3) shows real glossy mature units but cannot prove all glume veins or millimeter lengths.
tiles.short: Spikelet 2.2–3.7(–3.9) mm; lower glume 1/3–2/3, upper near full length.
tiles.status: REAL GLOSSY FRUIT PHOTO — MEASURED GLUME/LEMMA DISSECTION NEEDED

tiles.heading: 05 · PRACTICAL LOCAL LOOK-ALIKES
tiles.details: P. capillare is a hairy annual with a much more diffuse cloudlike head (different-species comparison panel 7, index 6, NOT Hall's panicgrass). Introduced P. coloratum is generally a coarser perennial forage grass; P. virgatum commonly has a taller rhizomatous base and conspicuous white blade-base hairs. Compare the true photographed Hall's ligule (index 5), rooted habit and mature spikelet. Neither a panicle silhouette nor blue-green color alone is decisive.
tiles.short: Contrast annual witchgrass, introduced kleingrass, and robust switchgrass.
tiles.status: REAL WITCHGRASS COMPARISON — MATCHED ANATOMY MISSING

tiles.heading: 06 · PUBLIC-READY GATE AND PHOTO/QA HANDOFF
tiles.details: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO (Grass Photo-Finish owning lane): same-specimen Hays-area connected rooted perennial crown, flowering stem and centimeter ruler; calibrated true 1–1.5-mm hair-fringe ligule/collar beside 1-mm scale (unscaled Uvalde ligule already photographed at index 5); two ripe 2.2–3.9-mm spikelets with individually separated glumes, sterile lemma and hard glossy awnless fertile lemma at 10–20×; matched local P. capillare, P. coloratum and P. virgatum comparisons where available. NEEDS_SITE_QA (Public Learner Readiness): verify all SIX physically archived exact-species JPEGs and their per-image rights (Commons CC BY/CC0, Jim Conrad's express public-domain release), seven total gallery panels including the DIFFERENT-SPECIES witchgrass at index 6, all SEVEN existing visible-structure arrows, gallery indexing, credits and mobile Pages rendering. Preserve taxonomy/subspecies/county holds; do not claim measured anatomy or FINISHED from unscaled photos.
tiles.short: FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS: six archived exact-species JPEGs; measured reproductive dissection and connected root still missing.

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: HALL'S PANICGRASS: Look first for a small stiff, often blue-green perennial basal tuft with curled old leaves and an orderly open 6–20 cm panicle. Six physically archived exact-species photos now include Jim Conrad's actual Uvalde limestone-site tufts and WHITE TRUE LIGULE HAIR FRINGE at the leaf/sheath junction. The photographed hair fringe is a real field clue, NOT a ruler-verified 1–1.5 mm measurement or proof of a connected Hays root crown. Confirm the glossy awnless fertile lemma and glumes from measured mature spikelets; separate from hairy annual witchgrass, introduced kleingrass and switchgrass.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: START with the physically archived whole-habit photograph: trace the relatively small mostly basal perennial tuft and stiff ascending panicle branches; do not infer a rhizome from the photo.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Jim Conrad's source-authenticated Uvalde photograph (species panel 6, index 5) ACTUALLY SHOWS a white fringe of true ligule hairs at the blade/sheath junction, with the comparatively smooth green sheath below; two arrows target these visible tissues. This is genuine anatomical photo evidence but the original is unscaled, so the Kew species-level 1–1.5 mm hair-fringe length remains a PUBLISHED measurement, not photo-measured. A Williamson County subsp. filipes treatment describes a 1.2–1.5 mm membranous ciliate ligule and pale collar; do not impose subspecies-specific morphology or identity on this species-level photo. Still obtain a calibrated 1-mm collar image of a connected local specimen.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Species panel 3 (index 2) shows actual branch architecture and small attached spikelets, with existing arrows only on visible units. Kew reports appressed solitary spikelets; Williamson subsp. filipes specimens can show short paired stalks, so do not force an unexamined subspecies arrangement onto this species card. A very diffuse detached/tumbling annual head suggests P. capillare instead.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: Panicum virgatum: Switchgrass is much taller and rhizomatous with a much larger diffuse panicle. Panicum capillare: Witchgrass is annual and strongly hairy with a huge lax panicle; Hall's is perennial, glaucous and stiffer.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

field_rule: Small blue-green perennial basal tuft + relatively orderly ascending-branched panicle + measured true hairy/ciliate ligule and hard shiny mature fertile lemma. No single habit photograph proves the species.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
